text:
maria: heads up — support ticket from AcmeX: generation API p99 spiked from ~320ms -> ~1.8s starting ~03:00 UTC after last infra deploy. Customer attached traces and says it affects only long-context requests (seq > 1024) and sometimes fails with 503. Filing here to triage. :rotating_light:

alex: thanks, digging in. Which pool/region? and did they pin model version or are we routing to quantized variants?

maria: customer on hosted-us-west, model: rwlm-large-v1 (not quantized), traffic routed to gpu-pool-3. Not pinned — think they hit the new node image rolled 02:50 UTC.

sachin: I can see a correlated uptick in p95/p99 on gpu-pool-3 metrics around 02:45. p95 went from 180ms -> 620ms, p99 from 320ms -> 1.8s. CPU host load modest but NVMe latency looks noisy. Sample from iostat: 

```
Device:         r/s     w/s    rKB/s    wKB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await  r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200    400   96000    32000   80.0     2.6     18.3   2.0     24.5   0.20   98.5
```

jia: that avgqu-sz of 2.6 and util ~98% is alarming. Could be IO contention or a change in write pattern. Any chance the new driver/firmware changed the NVMe queue handling?

alex: last node image included the driver bump to NVIDIA 535.54 and kernel 6.4.8. We also pushed a small change to our checkpointing: more aggressive KV-cache flush frequency (to avoid memory growth) which increased disk writes.

leo: putting hypotheses: (1) driver+kernel change affected DMA scheduling causing higher tail latency; (2) increased flush frequency created IO bursts; (3) background GC on the SSD coincided.

oncall-bot: @maria — incident created: INC-20250313-47. Pager duty notify sent.

maria: reproduction steps from customer (I ran locally against staging):

1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwlm-large-v1","input":"<~2k tokens prompt>","max_tokens":1024}' 
2) observe p99 ~1.6s on staging-gpu-3 when sequence >1024 and batch_size=1. Lowering max_tokens to 256 returns p99 ~320ms.

sachin: interesting — suggests per-token or kv-cache growth interacts badly with IO. Do we spill KV cache to disk at certain sizes?

alex: yes, we shard KV cache to tmpfs but fallback to disk happens for large sequences when memory budget exceeded. The fallback path uses async write to NVMe which was tweaked in last runtime patch (we switched to aio_submit path matched to new kernel's submission model).

jia: if the aio_submit path has a regression with new driver/kernel combo, we could be falling back to slower io_uring or causing serializing submissions. Let's gather kernel dmesg for affected hosts and NVMe firmware versions.

leo: pulled dmesg from node gpu-3-14: multiple messages: 

```
[02:52:11] nvme nvme0: I/O submitted with bad queue size, falling back to sync io
[02:52:12] nvme nvme0: timeout waiting for completion, qid=3
[02:52:13] audit: type=1400 apparmor="DENIED" operation="open" profile="/usr/bin/runtime" name="/tmp/kvcache/large-..." pid=18456 comm="runtime" scontext=unconfined
```

alex: that first line matches what I feared. There's a mismatch in submission path assumptions. For immediate mitigation we can: (A) pin affected customers to CPU-quantized variant (uses less KV and avoids disk spills), (B) temporarily reduce KV-cache flush frequency to pre-patch value, (C) roll nodes in gpu-pool-3 back to driver 525.xx image. Thoughts?

maria: customer needs low-latency — prefer (A) + (B) quick, and (C) if (A)/(B) not working then rollback. I'll offer (A) now to the customer as a temporary config change.

sachin: implement (B) now — I'll patch runtime config on gpu-pool-3 to increase the memory threshold from 8GB -> 12GB before spilling. That should reduce immediate IO bursts.

jia: I'll start a canary rollback of driver on one node (gpu-3-14) to 525.85 to validate if NVMe errors stop. If rollback removes the nvme I/O warnings, it's strong signal to roll entire pool.

leo: work items captured in INC-20250313-47. Also add to eng-runtime backlog: revert async write change and add unit/integration test that exercises large-KV path under new kernels.

maria: update: offered customer CPU-quantized route and they accepted; we toggled routing for their API key to cpu-fallback route at 03:25 UTC. Their p99 dropped to ~360ms. Customer is happy for now but wants root cause.

alex: rollback canary completed — nvme warnings disappeared on gpu-3-14 and avgqu-sz dropped to 0.6, p99 on that node back to 330ms. So driver/kernel combo + aio_submit tweak likely triggered the regression.

jia: next steps I'm proposing:
- full rollback of driver on gpu-pool-3 (coord with infra deploy window)
- revert runtime async write patch and re-evaluate io_uring vs aio_submit on kernel 6.4.8
- add telemetry to surface KV spill counts per request and per-host (to correlate spills -> latency)
- add automated stresstest for long-context generation to CI that runs on both new and old kernels

sachin: also add a temporary runtime feature-flag to force in-memory only for pinned customers until we've validated IO path under new driver.

maria: I'll send a customer postmortem update indicating mitigation and planned rollback timeline. Also scheduling a follow-up with infra and runtime teams at 10:00 PT to coordinate full pool fix.

leo: small note — check NVMe firmware mismatch across hosts; mixed firmware sometimes surfaces after driver change. If we find mixed firmware, coordinate with vendors for patch.

alex: ack. I'll prepare the rollback playbook and coordinate with fleet to avoid mass restarts.

oncall-bot: INC-20250313-47 updated: status -> mitigated, mitigations: routing to cpu-fallback, patched runtime threshold, rollback canary successful.

maria: thanks team. I'll keep thread open until pool rollback is complete and we have a root cause write-up. :eyes:
